# UMC: guidance audit and operating valuation anchors

As of 19 October 2026. Research package only; no website or canonical data publication performed.

## Main findings

The operating record is more nuanced than a single guidance hit rate. Quarterly shipment guidance was often conservative, but pricing and gross-margin forecasts were not uniformly conservative. The company primarily guides using qualitative expressions, so a precise aggregate accuracy score would be misleading.

The package pairs the original prior-quarter outlook with the subsequently reported result for ten completed quarters, Q1 2024–Q2 2026. It includes 40 operating comparisons and ten annual-capex references. The capex references are deliberately not treated as ten independent quarterly forecasts. FY2024 and FY2025 are the two completed annual spending outcomes.

Q3 2026 operating guidance remains pending. The issuer scheduled the results call for 28 October. However, July–September monthly sales are already available: the sum is NT$74.239117bn, up 8.0114% sequentially and 25.5587% year over year. That is a valid revenue run-rate input, not evidence of Q3 gross margin, ASP, wafer shipments or utilization. [Monthly sales](https://www.umc.com/en/IR_Financial/monthly_sales_revenue); [October 13 filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526419602/umc-ex99.htm).

## Ten-quarter view

Percentages below are percentages, not basis points. Shipment changes are quarter over quarter. Approximate/qualitative wording is preserved; brackets and numerical scoring bands have not been invented. The machine-readable files include issue dates, original wording, actual dates, exact source URLs, page references and comparison explanations.

| Quarter | Prior shipment outlook → actual | Prior USD ASP outlook → actual report | Prior gross-margin outlook → actual | Prior utilization outlook → actual |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 2024 | approximately +2–3% → +4.5% | -5% → declined, magnitude unreported | approximately 30% → 30.9% | low-60% → 65% |
| Q2 2024 | low-single-digit growth → +2.6% | firm → firm | approximately 30% → 35.2% | mid-60% → 68% |
| Q3 2024 | mid-single-digit growth → +7.8% | firm → firm | mid-30% → 33.8% | approximately 70% → 71% |
| Q4 2024 | flat → +1.5% | flat → flat | close to 30% → 30.4% | high-60% → 70% |
| Q1 2025 | flat → flat | mid-single-digit decline → declined, magnitude unreported | >25%, including earthquake impact → 26.7% | approximately 70% → 69% |
| Q2 2025 | +5–7% → +6.2% | flat → firm | approximately 30% → 28.7% | mid-70% → 76% |
| Q3 2025 | low-single-digit growth → +3.4% | firm → firm | approximately Q2's 28.7%, subject to FX → 29.8% | mid-70% → 78% |
| Q4 2025 | flat → -0.6% | firm → firm | high-20% → 30.7% | mid-70% → 78% |
| Q1 2026 | flat → +2.7% | firm → declined | high-20% → 29.2% | mid-70% → 79% |
| Q2 2026 | high-single-digit growth → +10.6% | low-single-digit growth → increased, magnitude unreported | approximately 30% → 32.5% | low-80% → 85% |

All original reports and decks were retrieved from the [issuer quarterly archive](https://www.umc.com/en/Download/quarterly_results/QuarterlyResults). Q4 2023 is included as the source of the Q1 2024 forecast. Reports contain written management commentary, but no issuer-authored full Q&A transcript was located. The Q2 2026 webcast page lists the report, presentation and abbreviated financial statements; it does not list a transcript. Audio was not transcribed. Therefore exact ASP movements or additional Q&A estimates have not been silently filled from third-party transcripts.

### Interpretation

- Shipment upside is clear in Q1 and Q3 2024 and Q2 2026. UMC itself described Q3 2024 shipments as stronger than expected. Flat guidance is not the same as an exact 0.000% numerical forecast, so +1.5%, -0.6% and +2.7% results retain contextual labels rather than arbitrary hit/miss thresholds.
- Q1 2026 is a clear directional pricing exception: reported ASP declined versus a firm outlook. Management attributed part of the decline to higher 8-inch shipment mix.
- Q2 2025 gross margin was 28.7% against an approximately 30% outlook. Currency sensitivity matters. Q3 2025's original margin outlook explicitly contained an FX qualification.
- Two comparisons allow strict numerical scoring without additional tolerance assumptions: Q2 2025 shipment growth met the 5–7% band, and Q1 2025 margin exceeded the 25% floor. This small subset must not be marketed as a 100% overall guidance accuracy record. Q1 2024 shipment growth exceeded the stated approximate 2–3% endpoints, but the issuer did not define a tolerance for “approximately.”

## Capital deployment and timing

FY2024 cash capex was reported as US$2.9bn versus an initial US$3.3bn budget, reduced to US$3.0bn in October 2024. FY2025 actual spending was US$1.6bn versus US$1.8bn guidance. Rounded annual figures differ slightly from summed quarterly spending, US$2.858bn and US$1.616bn respectively. Lower capex is not automatically an operating “miss”; timing and capacity discipline must be assessed separately.

FY2026 guidance increased from US$1.5bn to US$2.0bn on 29 July. H1 spending was US$724m. The US$1.276bn H2 residual is arithmetic, not a separate forecast. Latest capex mix is 90% for 12-inch and 10% for 8-inch. [Q2 2026 report](https://www.umc.com/upload/media/08_Investors/Financials/Quarterly_Results/Quarterly_2020-2029_English_pdf/2026/Q2_2026/UMC26Q2_report.pdf), p9.

Project execution deserves a different lens from near-term quarterly guidance. The original Singapore P3 announcement targeted late-2024 production with 30,000 wafers/month and a US$5bn project. The April 2025 inauguration release instead targeted volume production in 2026. This is a documented schedule shift; it is not appropriate to continue presenting the original date as current. Customer multi-year supply agreements support demand visibility, but do not establish that the project is fully prepaid. [Original P3 plan](https://www.umc.com/en/News/press_release/Content/corporate/20220224-1); [inauguration and revised target](https://www.umc.com/en/News/press_release/Content/corporate/20250401).

The July 2026 board approval authorized NT$148.68bn of capacity deployment, funded from working capital. It covers phased Singapore P4 cleanroom/tool expansion and the Tainan building shell for future P7/P8. This is not the FY2026 cash-capex number. The company stresses sequencing against secured customer commitments; a complete multi-year cash schedule and location split are not disclosed. [SEC Exhibit 99.2](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526322027/umc-ex99.htm).

Intel collaboration uses existing Ocotillo Arizona infrastructure and a jointly developed 12nm FinFET process, with 2027 production expected in the primary materials. Neither the official release nor UMC's current technology page quantifies UMC's revenue share or profit margin. Any meaningful 2027/2028 revenue ramp in a valuation is an analyst scenario. [Intel announcement](https://www.intc.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1671/intel-and-umc-announce-new-foundry-collaboration); [UMC technology page](https://www.umc.com/en/Product/technologies/Index/).

Silicon photonics is beyond a purely conceptual milestone: UMC and SILITH announced first mass-production wafer delivery in July 2026. The broader UMC platform is targeted for customer development in 2027. Neither milestone provides a reliable standalone revenue forecast. [Joint announcement](https://www.umc.com/en/News/press_release/Content/technology_related/20260714).

## DCF guardrails

1. Use operating income and normalized operating cash flows. Q2 2026 attributable net income of NT$42.260bn includes NT$30.236bn of non-operating income; net investment gain was NT$30.045bn. Operating income was NT$14.950bn. Associates/JVs supplied NT$23.606bn of profit in the quarterly cash-flow reconciliation. A model annualizing NT$42.26bn quarterly earnings would capitalize investment gains as if recurring foundry cash earnings. The capital-structure companion research supplies the investee-level bridge.
2. Capacity and shipments are different measures. Reported Q2 utilization is 85% and uses production output divided by capacity. Do not recompute it from shipments of 1.129m divided by capacity of 1.305m 12-inch-equivalent wafers.
3. Mix denominators matter. Region, technology and application tables describe wafer sales. “Others” is not an automotive-only segment. Q2 wafer-sales mix was 37% at 22/28nm and 52% at 40nm and below. The separately reported 22nm contribution reached 17.5% of quarter sales.
4. FX conventions changed. Q1/Q2 2026 translated income-statement figures use weighted-average NTD/USD rates of 31.63 and 31.59. The June 30 condensed balance sheet uses 31.84. Earlier releases used period-end currency conversions. Do not interpret movement in the convenience-translated USD revenue series as exact ASP changes; use a separately dated valuation FX rate.
5. Headline tax is not normalized operating tax. Q2 effective tax was approximately 6.56% and H1 approximately 5.64%. H1 also includes a NT$1.947bn deferred-tax benefit associated with the renewed Taiwan–Singapore agreement. Singapore incentives granted in 2025 extend to July 2035. The renewed treaty takes effect on 1 January 2027; tax-sparing ceases after three taxable years, which the issuer says will increase future effective tax rates. No exact forward ETR was located. A 20–25% normalized cash-tax assumption, if used by the valuation, is explicitly an analyst assumption. [June financial notes](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526322030/umc-ex99_1.htm), note 6(26), printed pp51–53.
6. Financing is not free cash. June balances include NT$40.045bn guarantee deposits and NT$6.214bn contract liabilities; H1 asset-grant cash receipts were NT$3.781bn. These are not all proven to be Singapore funding, and should not automatically be treated as nonrecurring-free operating cash flow or surplus equity. Construction commitments at June 30 predate the July expansion approval.
7. Avoid press-estimate contamination. UMC's October 7 clarification declined to comment on press estimates of approximately 21% revenue growth and 133% profit growth in 2026. These figures are explicitly not management guidance. [October filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1033767/000119312526419602/umc-ex99.htm), Exhibit 99.1.

## Files and reproducibility

- guidance_vs_actual.json / .csv: 50 observations, original guidance, actuals, dates, source IDs/URLs/pages and conservative comparison labels.
- quarterly_operating_facts.json / .csv: ten-quarter operating, capex, region, node and end-market data.
- annual_capex_track_record.json: two completed annual outcomes and pending FY2026 budget revision.
- pending_guidance.json: Q3 2026 forecast and pending-status evidence.
- monthly_sales_cutoff.json / .csv: monthly sales through September and explicit arithmetic aggregates.
- dcf_operating_anchors.json / .csv: source-linked actuals, issuer projections, and model-use cautions.
- guidance_qa.json: coverage, missing numeric ASPs, mix-total checks and source-hash verification.
- source_manifest_complete.json: exact original URLs, retrieval times, SHA-256 hashes and private frozen paths.
- private-sources/: source originals and local text extractions. These are research evidence only and must not be published or included in a public build.

The Python scripts preserve derivation logic. Run order is collect_sources.py, collect_expansions.py, build_guidance.py, build_anchors.py, add_monthly.py. Re-fetching updates retrieval timestamps and may change source bytes; the delivered frozen snapshot is the auditable cutoff package. Rebuilding anchors before reapplying monthly updates removes the two later monthly/press anchors, so preserve the stated order.
